title: Twice Sequential Monte Carlo for Tree Search
claim: Our search method keeps improving with more sequential compute while baselines plateau, with higher variance and collapsing diversity.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared x-axis, confidence bands
description: Three side-by-side line plots share the x-axis, Search Depth Budget, at 2, 4, 6, 12, 16 and 24. The left panel, Performance Scaling with Depth, plots AUC of normalized returns. The green TSMCTS (ours) curve climbs to about 0.68. The teal SMCTS curve and the red SMC baseline curve plateau at about 0.4 and 0.35. The center panel plots variance of the root estimator. The red baseline and the purple TRT SMC curve are high, at about 10 and 5. The green and teal curves stay near 0 to 1. The right panel, Path Degeneracy at the Root, plots active actions in the target. Green stays flat at 4, teal and purple stay near 2.9, and red collapses to 1. Shaded bands show confidence intervals. The green ours curve is the focus. Legends sit inside the panels.
caption: Left: Performance scaling with depth (higher is better), averaged across environments, particle budgets of $4, 8, 16$ and 10 seeds. Center: Variance of the root estimator vs. depth (lower is better). Right: The number of actions active in the policy target (higher is better, constant is better). Center and right are averaged across states and particle budgets $4, 8, 16$ and 5 seeds, in Snake. Mean and $95%$ Gaussian CI for all curves.
abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods that leverage search are responsible for many milestone breakthroughs in RL. Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) recently emerged as an alternative to the Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithm which drove these breakthroughs. SMC is easier to parallelize and more suitable to GPU acceleration. However, it also suffers from large variance and path degeneracy which prevent it from scaling well with increased search depth, i.e., increased sequential compute. To address these problems, we introduce Twice Sequential Monte Carlo Tree Search (TSMCTS). Across discrete and continuous environments TSMCTS outperforms the SMC baseline as well as a popular modern version of MCTS as a policy improvement operator, scales favorably with sequential compute, reduces estimator variance and mitigates the effects of path degeneracy while retaining the properties that make SMC natural to parallelize.
